Each lab has an **overview page** (why it matters, key concepts, what you'll do) and two parallel versions of the code: an **R notebook** (`.qmd`) and a **Python notebook** (`.ipynb`). They follow the same steps, so you can work in either language, or compare the two side by side.

::: {.callout-tip title="First time here?"}
Follow [Get set up](../setup.qmd) to download a starter kit with every lab and the course data. Python notebooks can also run on Google Colab with nothing to install.
:::

:::{#lab-list}
:::

## Demos

Shorter, instructor-led examples used in class: a model bake-off with partial dependence plots, marginal vs. partial effects, information leakage in evaluation, and sampling from a point process. See the [demos page](demos.qmd).

## Packages by lab

| Lab | R | Python |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · Simulation | terra, ggplot2, ggcorrplot | numpy, pandas, matplotlib, statsmodels |
| 2 · Evaluation | caret, pROC, PRROC, blockCV | scikit-learn, statsmodels |
| 3 · CART | rpart, rpart.plot, pROC | scikit-learn |
| 4 · Random forests | randomForest, ranger, caret, pROC | scikit-learn |
| 5 · Boosted trees | gbm, dismo, pROC | scikit-learn |
| 6 · Maxent | maxnet (+ Maxent Java app) | elapid (+ Maxent Java app) |
| 7 · Neural networks (bonus) | neuralnet, pROC | scikit-learn |

Every R lab also uses **terra** and **here**. Every Python lab also uses **numpy**, **pandas**, **matplotlib**, and the course helper **sdmlab**.
